findings.problem: Column-evidence inconsistency: the document line contains 8 values (74.4, 80.8, 82.9, 87.6, 80.2, -, 80.5, 80.6), but the column evidence says the extraction read 'all 6 comparison values' and matched column '**Nex-N2-mini**' at cell position 1. The stated header column is one of 8 columns implied by the row; matching the first cell to a header whose identity and position cannot be verified against 13 intervening lines is not established by the supplied evidence. The check-3 requirement that the quoted column is this model's column, not a neighbouring one, is therefore unverified for an unmatched source identity.

Benchmark/value ambiguity in the column evidence: the document line is 'SWE-bench Multimodal 38.4 34.5 - -' and the value 34.5 percent is claimed as the cell under column 'Claude Opus 4.7'. The evidence states only 'exactly one matching value' and matches by column position; it does not identify which of the two present columns (38.4 or 34.5) is Claude Opus 4.7. Also the value 34.5 is the second data cell while the header 'Claude Opus 4.7' is said to be above the row without a stated offset, so a neighbouring column cannot be excluded from the supplied evidence.

Column-evidence inconsistency: the document line has 6 values (69.3, 69.3, 51.7, 77.5, 67.2, 71.3) but the column evidence says 'all 5 comparison values' were read, i.e. 6 total cells. 69.3 appears twice in the row, so the claimed value alone does not disambiguate the cell; the column 'Qwen3.5-397B-A17B' is asserted to be the header at position 1 with no verifiable offset for the '13 line(s) above' header. The named model is an unmatched source identity, and the source URL is a Qwen3.6-27B README, so column-to-value attribution is not independently established.

Internal inconsistency between candidate and supplied document line: the candidate is for benchmark 'swe-bench-multilingual' with model Claude Opus 5 and value 89.5, but the document line for the cited page 167 row is 'SWE-bench Multilingual 89.1 86.6 89.5 -'. Under the same source and page, candidate c2646aec2be3d1863d90 assigns 86.6 to 'Fable 5' and candidate c8044cfbff483b563df9 assigns 89.1 to 'Claude Fable 5.1/ Mythos 5.1', while this candidate assigns 89.5 to 'Claude Opus 5'. The row has only 3 comparison values; the differing claims about which header applies to which cell are mutually inconsistent and cannot all be reconciled from the supplied evidence.

Column-evidence inconsistency: the document line has 6 values but the column evidence says 'all 5 comparison values' were read; value 67.2 is the fifth cell and is also not unique across the slice. The column 'Qwen3.6-35B-A3B' is asserted at cell position 5 from a header 13 lines above, while the source is a Qwen3.6-27B README listing multiple Qwen models, so the header-to-value mapping is not verified by the supplied evidence.

Column-evidence inconsistency and ambiguity: the document line has 5 values (76.7, -, 77.8, 76.9*, 73.0) but the column evidence says 'exactly one matching value' for 76.7; the row also contains the differing variant '76.9*'. The header 'Kimi K2.6' is asserted 53 lines above the row, and no offset or neighboring-column check is supplied. A one-cell-tolerance misread (e.g., 76.7 vs 76.9*) cannot be excluded from the supplied evidence.

uncertainties: The column-evidence offsets (e.g. '13 line(s) above', '56 line(s) above') are self-reported by the extraction and cannot be independently confirmed without the captured documents' actual line layout; the supplied packet gives only a single claimed document line per candidate.
missing_evidence: Full column headers and their positions relative to each document line, sufficient to confirm that each quoted column name actually maps to the claimed value cell (check 3) for the multi-cell README rows.
